root_cause.text: RDMA drivers' rereg_mr paths reused an existing ib_umem on IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS without verifying that a read-only-pinned umem was still valid when access was upgraded to writable, allowing MR permissions to become RW without re-pinning/checking writable user memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds ib_umem_check_rereg() to reject `(IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS && !IB_MR_REREG_TRANS)` when `ib_access_writable(new_access_flags) && !umem->writable`, and inserts this check into multiple drivers' rereg_user_mr handlers; the commit message explicitly states that changing from RO to RW requires the umem to be re-evaluated to ensure it is properly pinned as RW.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an exported reregistration access check that blocks upgrading a reused non-writable umem to writable during access-only MR reregistration.
intent_record.what: A new exported function, ib_umem_check_rereg(struct ib_umem *umem, int flags, int new_access_flags), was added after ib_umem_copy_from(). The function returns 0 when umem is NULL, checks whether flags includes IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS but not IB_MR_REREG_TRANS, and if so returns -EACCES when new_access_flags request writable access while umem->writable is false; otherwise it returns 0.
intent_record.how: This adds a runtime validation helper for memory region re-registration that rejects access-only reregistration requests attempting to upgrade a reused umem from non-writable to writable. It allows drivers that reuse an existing umem during IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS to detect and prevent an invalid writable access change, while permitting other cases to proceed unchanged.

intent_record.how: This adds validation before allocating the command mailbox and proceeding with memory region re-registration, causing the function to fail early when the existing user memory and requested re-registration flags or access permissions are incompatible or invalid.

intent_record.how: At runtime, re-registration requests now undergo explicit validation of the existing user memory region, requested re-registration flags, and new access permissions before proceeding. Invalid or unsupported re-registration cases are rejected early with an error pointer instead of continuing into later logic.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause by validating MR re-registration access changes and preventing reuse of a non-writable existing ib_umem when access is upgraded to writable, rejecting invalid rereg requests before updates are applied.

The vulnerability is in MR re-registration handling, and these changes add early validation of user MR reregistration requests so invalid parameter combinations are rejected before reuse of existing umem/state. That directly aligns with preventing unsafe rereg paths like access upgrades without proper checks.

The change only introduces a local error-code variable in rxe_rereg_user_mr for future/error-handling support. It does not address the core vulnerability issue of validating or re-pinning ib_umem when access is upgraded to writable during rereg_mr.

The root cause is missing validation of UMEM during MR re-registration when access permissions change. Adding an exported declaration for checking UMEM re-registration parameters directly supports that validation logic, so it is tied to the vulnerability fix rather than unrelated refactoring.

This change directly pertains to the new ib_umem_check_rereg validation introduced to prevent unsafe MR re-registration access upgrades. Even though it is only a stub for non-CONFIG_INFINIBAND_USER_MEM builds, it supports the same vulnerability fix path and ensures the check fails safely with -EOPNOTSUPP when the feature is unavailable.

candidates.rationale: This conditional shows the pre-fix path only handled the case where ACCESS was not being changed; there was no corresponding validation when ACCESS was changed, enabling reuse of an existing umem without checking whether a read-only pin could be upgraded to writable.

This assignment reflects that the code carried forward access flags from the existing MR/umem state, contributing to reuse semantics without any check that the underlying ib_umem remained valid for upgraded writable access.
The pre-fix validation only rejected unsupported flag bits; it did not validate the dangerous supported case of ACCESS-only re-registration that upgrades permissions on a reused umem.

This shows the function was performing state updates for some reregistration cases without any early guard for invalid ACCESS changes, consistent with the vulnerable behavior of applying MR changes before validating reused umem writability.

The fix intent indicates an early abort was added in this function for invalid reregistration requests. While this line itself is not causative, the hunk lacks the exact pre-fix check statements; this candidate marks the affected function region where the missing validation existed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This branch handled only the non-ACCESS-rereg case, meaning there was no corresponding validation path when IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS was set. That omission allowed the code to reuse the existing ib_umem during an access upgrade without rechecking whether the user memory was valid for writable access.

This validation rejected only unsupported flag bits and did not reject the dangerous supported case of ACCESS-only re-registration. As a result, the path could proceed while reusing an existing ib_umem even when access permissions were upgraded to writable without re-pinning or validating writable memory.

This shows the function was proceeding with selective re-registration state changes without an early guard for invalid ACCESS changes. The missing validation allowed reused umem state to survive an access upgrade, enabling writable MR permissions without confirming the underlying memory was pinned writable.

This assignment preserved existing access flags from the current MR state as part of the reuse flow. In the vulnerable logic, that reuse occurred without validating whether the existing ib_umem, potentially pinned read-only, remained valid when permissions were changed toward writable access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function `mlx5_ib_rereg_user_mr()` contains the relevant rereg_mr access/umem reuse logic clearly enough to decide. The root cause was reusing an existing `ib_umem` on `IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS` when upgrading permissions without re-pinning/checking writable memory. In this snippet, the no-translation-change path (`if (!(flags & IB_MR_REREG_TRANS))`) only reuses the existing `mr->umem` when doing a pure PD/access update through `umr_rereg_pd_access()`, but only after checking `can_use_umr_rereg_access(dev, mr->access_flags, new_access_flags)`. More importantly, when translation changes or a new memory mapping is needed, the code does **not** blindly reuse the old umem for access upgrade: it explicitly obtains a fresh umem with `new_umem = ib_umem_get(&dev->ib_dev, start, length, new_access_flags);` before any PAS update or recreation. The fast PAS path uses this freshly pinned `new_umem` in `umr_rereg_pas(...)`, and the recreate path calls `create_real_mr(new_pd, new_umem, iova, new_access_flags)`. Also, when reusing the old umem to recreate without TRANS, the code first invalidates the old MR (`mlx5_mr_cache_invalidate(mr)`), detaches the umem from the old MR (`umem = mr->umem; mr->umem = NULL;`), and then passes it to `create_real_mr(...)`; it does not do an access-only upgrade on the old read-only-pinned umem. Thus the vulnerable construct of upgrading access while keeping an unchecked old umem is absent, and the fix is present because writable upgrades that need a new pin go through `ib_umem_get(..., new_access_flags)`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The added rereg path clearly shows the vulnerable construct. In `irdma_rereg_user_mr()`, when only access flags are changed, the code does `if (flags & IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS) iwmr->access = new_access;` and then, if `IB_MR_REREG_TRANS` is not set, it simply executes `ret = irdma_hwreg_mr(iwdev, iwmr, iwmr->access);`. There is no call to `ib_umem_get()` or any other re-pinning/revalidation of the existing `iwmr->region` for writable access in this access-only rereg case. The only place that obtains a new umem is `irdma_rereg_mr_trans()`, which is used only when `flags & IB_MR_REREG_TRANS` is set: `region = ib_umem_get(pd->device, start, len, iwmr->access);`. Therefore, an MR originally backed by a read-only-pinned `ib_umem` can have `iwmr->access` upgraded on `IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS` and be reprogrammed in hardware via `irdma_hwreg_mr()` while reusing the old umem without verifying writable pinning. That matches the root cause exactly. No fix is present here because there is no logic checking whether an existing umem remains valid when access is upgraded, nor any forced re-get/re-pin on `IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS`.
